# Attribution and licences

<!-- Generated by pipeline/manifest.py from pipeline/config.py. Edit those, not this file. -->

All anatomical geometry in this project is derived from published atlases distributed with
Lead-DBS. Nothing is hand-modelled. Coordinates are MNI ICBM 2009b nonlinear asymmetric (RAS, mm).

## Licence of the derived assets

The Lead-DBS `LICENSE.md` states that the standard-space atlases it ships are released under the
GNU GPL v3 at the request of their owners and should not be used for commercial purposes. The
meshes, streamline subsets and coordinates in `public/assets/` are derived from those atlases, so
they are distributed under **GPL-3.0, non-commercial**. The complete corresponding source (the
pipeline in `pipeline/`, which fetches the original files from the official Lead-DBS archive) is
part of this repository.

The ICBM 2009b T1, T2 and PD template slices carry the McGill/MNI notice:

> Copyright (C) 1993-2004 Louis Collins, McConnell Brain Imaging Centre, Montreal Neurological
> Institute, McGill University. Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software and its
> documentation for any purpose and without fee is hereby granted, provided that the above copyright
> notice appear in all copies. The authors and McGill University make no representations about the
> suitability of this software for any purpose. It is provided "as is" without express or implied warranty.

## Human Connectome Project data

Some tracts were generated from Human Connectome Project diffusion data and are therefore also
subject to the WU-Minn HCP Open Access Data Use Terms
(https://www.humanconnectome.org/study/hcp-young-adult/document/wu-minn-hcp-consortium-open-access-data-use-terms):
redistribution only under the same terms, acknowledgement when presenting results, and no attempt to
identify or contact participants.

- Confirmed HCP-derived: cst, ml, sw_pd, sw_dyt, sw_ts, sw_pd_m1, sw_pd_sma, sw_pd_pm (Hollunder 2024 sweet streamlines: connectome 'HCP 985 (Li 2020)' stated in the files; Meola 2016: HCP-488 data).
- Likely HCP-derived: hdp, al, lf, drtt, ndrtt (DBS Tractography Atlas family, whose later version is built on the HCP-1065 template; not stated for this version).

Required acknowledgement:

> Data were provided [in part] by the Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn Consortium (Principal Investigators: David Van Essen and Kamil Ugurbil; 1U54MH091657) funded by the 16 NIH Institutes and Centers that support the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research; and by the McDonnell Center for Systems Neuroscience at Washington University.

HCP methods to cite:

- Van Essen DC, Smith SM, Barch DM, Behrens TEJ, Yacoub E, Ugurbil K. The WU-Minn Human Connectome Project: An overview. NeuroImage. 2013;80:62-79. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.05.041.
- Glasser MF, Sotiropoulos SN, Wilson JA, Coalson TS, Fischl B, Andersson JL, et al. The minimal preprocessing pipelines for the Human Connectome Project. NeuroImage. 2013;80:105-124. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.04.127.
- Sotiropoulos SN, Jbabdi S, Xu J, Andersson JL, Moeller S, Auerbach EJ, et al. Advances in diffusion MRI acquisition and processing in the Human Connectome Project. NeuroImage. 2013;80:125-143. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2013.05.057.

## White-matter tracts section (HCP-1065)

The tracts in `public/assets/wm/` and `wm-manifest.json`, and the tract-to-region probabilities in
`src/data/generated/wm-connectome.json`, are derived from the HCP-1065 population-averaged
tractography atlas. They are **not** GPL-licensed Lead-DBS material: they carry the atlas licence,
CC BY-SA 4.0 (brain.labsolver.org/hcp_trk_atlas.html); derived from Human Connectome Project data, so also subject to the WU-Minn HCP Open Access Data Use Terms.
Share-alike: adapted versions of these files must be released under CC BY-SA 4.0 (or a compatible
licence) with attribution.

- Source: https://brain.labsolver.org/hcp_trk_atlas.html
- Note: Files from the 'hcp1065' release of github.com/data-others/atlas (hcp1065_avg_tracts_trk.zip; tract_to_region_connectome_BM_KL.xlsx). Space: ICBM 2009a nonlinear asymmetric (atlas page), shown here on the 2009b templates after an alignment check: along every tract the 2009b T1 is white-matter bright, and no shift of up to 2 mm in any direction raises it by more than 5% (pipeline/validate.py).
- Cite: Yeh FC. Population-based tract-to-region connectome of the human brain and its hierarchical topology. Nat Commun. 2022;13(1):4933. doi:10.1038/s41467-022-32595-4.
- Cite: Yeh FC, Panesar S, Fernandes D, Meola A, Yoshino M, Fernandez-Miranda JC, et al. Population-averaged atlas of the macroscale human structural connectome and its network topology. NeuroImage. 2018;178:57-68. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2018.05.027.
- Assets: wm_af, wm_slf1, wm_slf2, wm_slf3, wm_ifof, wm_ilf, wm_uf, wm_fat, wm_cing_fp, wm_cing_ph, wm_or, wm_cst, wm_cbt, wm_cc, wm_fx, wm_mdlf, wm_tpat, wm_vof, wm_emc, wm_ac, wm_atr, wm_str, wm_ptr, wm_ar, wm_cs_a, wm_cs_s, wm_cs_p, wm_scp, wm_mcp, wm_icp, wm_drtt, wm_ml, wm_rst, wm_cpt_f, wm_cpt_p, wm_cpt_o
- Changes made: streamlines subsampled and resampled, the corpus callosum cut at the midline, files
  converted to compressed glTF; connection probabilities kept as published (Brodmann block).
- HCP acknowledgement (required, as above):

> Data were provided [in part] by the Human Connectome Project, WU-Minn Consortium (Principal Investigators: David Van Essen and Kamil Ugurbil; 1U54MH091657) funded by the 16 NIH Institutes and Centers that support the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research; and by the McDonnell Center for Systems Neuroscience at Washington University.

## Skull base v1 (Z-Anatomy / BodyParts3D)

The meshes and lines in `public/assets/skullbase/` and the files `sb-manifest.json`, `sb-landmarks.json`,
`sb-regions.json` and `sb-definitions.json` are derived from Z-Anatomy, itself based on BodyParts3D. They are
**not** GPL-licensed: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Z-Anatomy); BodyParts3D CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan; definitions from Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0.

- Source: https://github.com/Z-Anatomy/Models-of-human-anatomy
- Note: One adult male model (BodyParts3D), not a population average, and not in MNI space. Coordinates are millimetres from Z-Anatomy's hypophysial fossa landmark. Bones were simplified (retopologized) by Z-Anatomy and are smoothed here by one subdivision level; vessels and nerves are drawn as tubes with the calibre Z-Anatomy models (not measured).
- Attribution: BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan
- Attribution: Z-Anatomy - The libre 3D atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0
- Attribution: Definitions: Wikipedia - CC-BY-SA 3.0 (the source page is linked on each definition)
- Cite: Mitsuhashi N, Fujieda K, Tamura T, Kawamoto S, Takagi T, Okubo K. BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Res. 2009;37(Database issue):D782-D785. doi:10.1093/nar/gkn613.
- Changes made: head structures exported from the Z-Anatomy Blender file (pipeline/skullbase_export.py), coordinates
  converted to mm from the hypophysial fossa landmark, midline structures cut at x = 0, bones smoothed by one subdivision
  level, decimated and shaded with baked ambient occlusion, vessels and nerves rebuilt as tubes with Z-Anatomy's modelled
  radius and cropped to the head, files converted to compressed glTF, definitions shortened to their lead section.

## Skull base v2 (TopBrain 2025 CT angiogram with Z-Anatomy fitted onto it)

The meshes in `public/assets/skullbase-ct/` and the files `sbct-manifest.json`, `sbct-landmarks.json`,
`sbct-regions.json` and `sbct-definitions.json` are derived from one CT angiogram of the TopBrain 2025 release and
from Z-Anatomy. They are **not** GPL-licensed: TopBrain data: open use with attribution, non-commercial (commercial use needs the data owner's permission; University Hospital Zurich); Z-Anatomy CC BY-SA 4.0, BodyParts3D CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan; definitions Wikipedia CC BY-SA 3.0.

- Source: https://topbrain2025.grand-challenge.org
- Note: One adult head CT angiogram (0.5 mm isotropic), not an average and not in MNI space. Bone (the cranial bones; the scan cuts the face off): the CT's own surface (400 HU, and thin bone down to 170 HU where it adjoins that bone, outside the labelled vessels, within TotalSegmentator's skull; and the walls of the air sinuses, where thin bone averaged with the air falls below any threshold; the holes this leaves in the paper-thin orbital roofs closed by rule at the height of the roof around them), named bone by bone after the nearest bone of the Z-Anatomy model fitted onto it. Arteries and the deep veins: surfaces of TopBrain's expert labels of the same scan. Cranial nerves, the dural sinuses and arteries TopBrain does not label, the soft tissue and the landmark names: the Z-Anatomy model fitted onto this skull (scaled, then deformed smoothly), so their positions are approximate. Coordinates: millimetres from the fitted hypophysial fossa, the CT turned into the Z-Anatomy model's frame.
- Attribution: TopBrain 2025 challenge data (University Hospital Zurich): CT angiogram and vessel labels of case topcow_ct_011 - https://topbrain2025.grand-challenge.org, https://zenodo.org/records/16878417 - open use, source given, non-commercial
- Attribution: BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan
- Attribution: Z-Anatomy - The libre 3D atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0
- Attribution: Definitions: Wikipedia - CC-BY-SA 3.0 (the source page is linked on each definition)
- Cite: Yang K, Shi P, Huang H, Musio F, Baazaoui H, Aydin OU, et al. TopBrain segmentation challenge for whole brain vessel anatomy. medRxiv. 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.05.28.26354312. Data: TopBrain 2025 challenge release, University Hospital Zurich, https://zenodo.org/records/16878417.
- Cite: Yang K, Musio F, Ma Y, Juchler N, Paetzold JC, Al-Maskari R, et al. The TopCoW challenge: topology-aware Circle of Willis segmentation for CT and MR angiography. NEJM AI. 2026;3(8). doi:10.1056/AIdbp2500994 (preprint arXiv:2312.17670).
- Cite: Mitsuhashi N, Fujieda K, Tamura T, Kawamoto S, Takagi T, Okubo K. BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Res. 2009;37(Database issue):D782-D785. doi:10.1093/nar/gkn613.
- Cite: Wasserthal J, Breit HC, Meyer MT, Pradella M, Hinck D, Sauter AW, et al. TotalSegmentator: Robust Segmentation of 104 Anatomic Structures in CT Images. Radiol Artif Intell. 2023;5(5):e230024. doi:10.1148/ryai.230024.
- Changes made: the CT's bone surface taken at 400 HU (thin bone down to 170 HU next to it, and the walls of the air sinuses) within TotalSegmentator's
  skull mask, the holes left in the thin orbital roofs closed by rule (a 1 mm plate at the height of the roof around them);
  skull mask, smoothed, decimated and named after the fitted Z-Anatomy bones; TopBrain's vessel labels meshed; the CT
  moved rigidly into the Z-Anatomy frame; Z-Anatomy's nerves, unlabelled vessels, soft tissue and landmarks scaled and
  smoothly deformed onto the CT's skull (pipeline/skullbase_ct.py); files converted to compressed glTF.

## Skull base, the default model ("v3" in the pipeline: the TopBrain CT with its anatomy made to fit it)

The meshes in `public/assets/skullbase-v3/` and the files `sbv3-manifest.json`, `sbv3-landmarks.json` and `sbv3-fit.json`
are derived from the OpenEar library of human temporal bones (CC BY 4.0); the page also shows Skull base v2's bone and
vessel files (TopBrain, see above). They are **not** GPL-licensed: TopBrain data: open use with attribution, non-commercial (University Hospital Zurich); OpenEar: CC BY 4.0; the nerves' courses derive from Z-Anatomy: CC BY-SA 4.0 (BodyParts3D CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan); definitions Wikipedia CC BY-SA 3.0 (as shipped with Z-Anatomy); TotalSegmentator segmentations (Apache-2.0 models); the surgical view's template brain: Lead-DBS, GPL-3.0 (FreeSurfer labels: research use).

- Source: https://zenodo.org/records/1473724
- Note: The bone and the labelled vessels are one adult's CT angiogram (TopBrain case 011); the cervical carotids, jugular veins and optic nerves are TotalSegmentator's segmentations of it. The temporal bone's contents (facial nerve, chorda tympani, cochleovestibular nerve, perilymphatic spaces, ossicles, tympanic membrane, petrous carotid) are a real ear's: OpenEar specimen ALPHA, registered onto each temporal bone of this CT, the left ear mirrored. The cranial nerves are routed through this CT's foramina from the Z-Anatomy model fitted onto it (their cisternal courses approximate). The greater petrosal nerve is drawn by rule. The surgical view's brain is a template (the Lead-DBS MNI 2009b pial surface, GPL-3.0) fitted into this CT, and its craniotomy is cut out of the CT's bone by rule.

- Changes made: specimen ALPHA's segmentations (facial nerve, chorda tympani, cochleovestibular nerve, scala tympani,
  scala vestibuli, ossicles, tympanic membrane, carotid) meshed (smoothed, decimated) and moved into the CT by a
  similarity registration of the specimen's bone onto each temporal bone, the left one mirrored
  (pipeline/skullbase_v3.py); landmarks derived from them; files converted to compressed glTF. The greater petrosal
  nerve is drawn by rule (the project's own, GPL-3.0). The cranial nerves are Z-Anatomy's fitted courses (CC BY-SA)
  rerouted through the CT's own foramina (pipeline/skullbase_v3_base.py); the optic nerves, cervical carotids and jugular
  veins are TotalSegmentator segmentations of the CT; the sigmoid and transverse sinuses are traced through its
  enhanced lumen, as is the petrous carotid; small arteries the CT cannot show are Z-Anatomy's fitted branches anchored to
  the CT's own parent vessels; foramina are located from the routes, the cranial floor's openings and the segmented carotid.
- Surgical views: the pterional, lateral supraorbital, parasagittal and midline suboccipital craniotomies are cut out of
  the CT's bone by rule (pipeline/skullbase_v3_approach.py, the project's own drawing, GPL-3.0). The brain (`br_*.glb`)
  is the Lead-DBS MNI 2009b pial surface (GPL-3.0, as in the cortex section; its FreeSurfer labels research use)
  decimated, deformed to fit this CT, pushed clear of its bone and vessels, split by lobe, with the right hemisphere's
  fissure opened, its frontal lobe lifted and the hemisphere held off the falx as morph targets
  (pipeline/skullbase_brain.py). The cerebellum, brainstem and fourth ventricle (`pf_*.glb`) are Z-Anatomy's (CC BY-SA
  4.0; BodyParts3D CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan) fitted into the CT's posterior fossa, the tonsils' retraction a morph target
  (pipeline/skullbase_pfossa.py); adapted, they stay under CC BY-SA.

## Brainstem section (Z-Anatomy fitted into MNI space; Harvard Ascending Arousal Network atlas 2.0)

The meshes in `public/assets/brainstem/` and the files `bs-manifest.json`, `bs-zones.json` and `bs-definitions.json`
are **not** GPL-licensed. The arousal network nuclei (`bs_aan_*.glb`) are derived from the Harvard Ascending Arousal
Network atlas 2.0 (CC0 1.0); everything else from Z-Anatomy, itself based on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA 4.0 (Z-Anatomy); BodyParts3D CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan; definitions from Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0).
The section also shows the white-matter section's tracts and the DBS section's deep nuclei, under their licences above.

- Source: https://github.com/Z-Anatomy/Models-of-human-anatomy
- Note: One adult model (BodyParts3D), fitted onto the ICBM 2009b template's brainstem: a similarity transform, then a smooth deformation, to the boundary between brainstem tissue and fluid on the T2 template. The surface follows the template closely; nerves, arteries and the nuclei inside are carried along, so their positions are approximate (the model's nuclei are simple shapes).
- Attribution: BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan
- Attribution: Z-Anatomy - The libre 3D atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0
- Attribution: Definitions: Wikipedia - CC-BY-SA 3.0 (the source page is linked on each definition)
- Cite: Mitsuhashi N, Fujieda K, Tamura T, Kawamoto S, Takagi T, Okubo K. BodyParts3D: 3D structure database for anatomical concepts. Nucleic Acids Res. 2009;37(Database issue):D782-D785. doi:10.1093/nar/gkn613.
- Cite: Fonov V, Evans AC, Botteron K, Almli CR, McKinstry RC, Collins DL. Unbiased average age-appropriate atlases for pediatric studies. NeuroImage. 2011;54(1):313-327. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.07.033.
- Source: https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.zw3r228d2
- Note: Ten brainstem nuclei of the ascending arousal network, annotated on ex vivo MRI with histology, in MNI152 space at 1 mm.
- Attribution: Edlow BL, Kinney HC (2023). Harvard Ascending Arousal Network Atlas - Version 2.0. Dryad. CC0 1.0
- Cite: Edlow BL, Kinney HC. Harvard Ascending Arousal Network Atlas – Version 2.0 [dataset]. Dryad; 2023. doi:10.5061/dryad.zw3r228d2.
- Cite: Olchanyi MD, Augustinack J, Haynes RL, et al. Automated MRI segmentation of brainstem nuclei critical to consciousness. Hum Brain Mapp. 2025;46(14):e70357. doi:10.1002/hbm.70357.
- Changes made: the brainstem, its surface features, ventricles, cranial nerve nuclei, cranial nerves III-XII and the
  arteries around it exported from the Z-Anatomy Blender file (pipeline/brainstem_export.py) and fitted into MNI space
  onto the ICBM 2009b T2 template (pipeline/brainstem_fit.py); nerves and arteries rebuilt as tubes and kept near the
  brainstem; safe entry zones drawn by rule on the fitted surface; the AAN labels' surfaces taken after resampling to
  0.5 mm; midline structures cut at x = 0; files converted to compressed glTF; definitions shortened to their lead
  section.

## Ventricles section (TopBrain 2025 CT angiogram, case 011)

The ventricle meshes in `public/assets/ventricles/` and `ve-manifest.json`, `ve-landmarks.json` and `ve-trajectories.json`
are derived from the TopBrain CT (TopBrain data: open use with attribution, non-commercial (University Hospital Zurich)): **not** GPL-licensed. The section also shows Skull base v2's bone and
Skull base v3's fitted brain, under their licences above.

- Source: https://zenodo.org/records/16878417
- Note: One adult's CT angiogram (TopBrain 2025 case 011, Skull base v2's): the bone and these ventricles are this patient's; the brain around them is a template fitted into the CT (Skull base v3). Teaching tool, not for planning.
- Attribution: TopBrain 2025 challenge data (University Hospital Zurich): CT angiogram and vessel labels of case topcow_ct_011 - https://topbrain2025.grand-challenge.org, https://zenodo.org/records/16878417 - open use, source given, non-commercial
- Cite: Yang K, Shi P, Huang H, Musio F, Baazaoui H, Aydin OU, et al. TopBrain segmentation challenge for whole brain vessel anatomy. medRxiv. 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.05.28.26354312. Data: TopBrain 2025 challenge release, University Hospital Zurich, https://zenodo.org/records/16878417.
- Changes made: the lateral and third ventricles segmented from the CT by a threshold in its brain window
  (pipeline/ventricles_build.py); the coronal suture, Kocher's points and the external acoustic meatus located on the
  CT; ventriculostomy trajectories computed on it; files converted to compressed glTF.

## Cortex section (Destrieux parcellation on the Lead-DBS template surface)

The meshes in `public/assets/cortex/` and `ctx-manifest.json` / `ctx-labels.json` are derived from the Lead-DBS
MNI 2009b template surface and the FreeSurfer annotations (Destrieux aparc.a2009s, Desikan-Killiany aparc)
shipped with it. Licence: GPL-3.0, non-commercial (derived from the Lead-DBS template surface and the FreeSurfer annotations shipped with it; FreeSurfer: MGH licence, research use); definition texts CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikipedia, via Z-Anatomy).

- Source: https://www.lead-dbs.org
- Note: One template brain (MNI ICBM 2009b nonlinear asymmetric average), not an individual. Labels from FreeSurfer's automatic Destrieux parcellation of that template, as shipped with Lead-DBS. Surfaces decimated to 80k faces per hemisphere; the inflated surface is computed by smoothing the pial surface.
- Cite: Destrieux C, Fischl B, Dale A, Halgren E. Automatic parcellation of human cortical gyri and sulci using standard anatomical nomenclature. NeuroImage. 2010;53(1):1–15. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2010.06.010.
- Cite: Neudorfer C, Butenko K, Oxenford S, Rajamani N, Achtzehn J, Goede L, et al. Lead-DBS v3.0: Mapping deep brain stimulation effects to local anatomy and global networks. NeuroImage. 2023;268:119862. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2023.119862.
- Lobe grouping: Klein A, Tourville J. Front Neurosci. 2012;6:171 (CC BY 3.0). doi:10.3389/fnins.2012.00171.
- Names, views and mean areas: Table 1 of Destrieux et al. 2010.
- Definitions: Wikipedia - CC-BY-SA 3.0, as shipped with Z-Anatomy (each links its source page).
- Changes made: surfaces decimated and split by label, an inflated surface and sulcal-depth shading computed,
  files converted to compressed glTF; definitions shortened to their lead section.

## Spine section (VerSe CT with TotalSegmentator segmentations)

The meshes in `public/assets/spine/` and the files `spine-manifest.json` and `spine-levels.json` are derived from
one CT of the VerSe 2020 dataset. They are **not** GPL-licensed: CC BY-SA 4.0 (VerSe); segmentations made here with TotalSegmentator (Apache-2.0 models) from the same CT.

- Source: https://osf.io/4skx2/
- Note: One adult whole-body trauma CT from the VerSe 2020 dataset (0.72 x 0.72 x 0.7 mm), not an average and not in MNI space. Coordinates are millimetres from the centre of the L5 vertebral body. Vertebrae C1-L5: surfaces taken from the CT at 200 HU within reach of VerSe's hand-corrected masks. Sacrum, pelvis, discs and spinal canal contents: TotalSegmentator segmentations of the same CT.
- Cite: Löffler MT, Sekuboyina A, Jacob A, Grau AL, Scharr A, El Husseini M, et al. A Vertebral Segmentation Dataset with Fracture Grading. Radiol Artif Intell. 2020;2(4):e190138. doi:10.1148/ryai.2020190138.
- Cite: Liebl H, Schinz D, Sekuboyina A, Malagutti L, Löffler MT, Bayat A, et al. A computed tomography vertebral segmentation dataset with anatomical variations and multi-vendor scanner data. Sci Data. 2021;8(1):284. doi:10.1038/s41597-021-01060-0.
- Cite: Sekuboyina A, Husseini ME, Bayat A, Löffler M, Liebl H, Li H, et al. VerSe: A Vertebrae labelling and segmentation benchmark for multi-detector CT images. Med Image Anal. 2021;73:102166. doi:10.1016/j.media.2021.102166.
- Cite: Wasserthal J, Breit HC, Meyer MT, Pradella M, Hinck D, Sauter AW, et al. TotalSegmentator: Robust Segmentation of 104 Anatomic Structures in CT Images. Radiol Artif Intell. 2023;5(5):e230024. doi:10.1148/ryai.230024.
- Changes made: bone surfaces from the CT within reach of the VerSe masks, TotalSegmentator segmentations of the
  same CT, meshes smoothed, decimated and split at the midline, schematic roots and psoas zones drawn by rule,
  coordinates moved to the centre of the L5 vertebral body, files converted to compressed glTF.
- The virtual screw's files (`public/assets/spine/screw_*.bin.gz`, `spine-screw.json`: distance fields of the
  bone, points on the structures at risk, pedicle measurements) are derived from the same CT and segmentations
  and carry the same licence.

`spine-published.json` holds published pedicle values read from the tables of three open-access papers (cited
on the cards and the Sources page): Wang 2023 (J Orthop Surg Res, CC BY 4.0), Moncada-Habib 2025 (Cureus,
CC BY 4.0) and Nkwerem 2024 (J West Afr Coll Surg, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); numbers only, no text or figures.

## Datasets considered and not used

- **Basal Ganglia Pathway Atlas, original files (Petersen 2019, OSF mhd4z).** The OSF terms limit use to
  academic research by the users under an agreement with CWRU and grant no redistribution, so the raw
  files are not used. Its pathways reach this project only through the Lead-DBS-distributed Dystonia
  Response Tract Atlas (Horn 2022).
- **DBS Tractography Atlas v2.1 (github.com/netstim/DBS-Tractography-Atlas).** The repository has no
  licence file, so redistribution rights are unclear. The Lead-DBS-distributed version (Middlebrooks 2020)
  is used instead.
- **Rajamani 2024 symptom-specific PD tracts.** Not distributed as files (the paper releases the
  DBS Tractography Atlas and source data, not the tract library). The PD symptom views show derived
  subsets of the Hollunder 2024 PD sweet streamlines instead, labelled as such.
- **Hammersmith atlas (Lead-DBS).** Its licence forbids redistribution; not used.
